name: Southwest Route (South Peak)
pitch_detail: Above the basin, travel is class 3-4 scrambling and, in early season, snow patches reported at roughly 35-40 degrees, broken by short roped sections including a class 5.0 ramp and a 5.6 crux bulge/wall, before class 2-4 terrain leads to the summit ridge.
descent_text: Descend the line you climbed. From the summit, reverse the narrow west ridge: the short 5.6 headwall below the top is usually rappelled from the anchor on the platform above it, and the overhang lower on the ridge is rappelled from a fixed bolt. Between those the crest is loose, with scree-covered ledges where a slip is serious, and most of the traverse is on the south side of the ridge. Past the overhang, go back around the rib and the broad loose gully to the access notch and drop to the 6,800 ft saddle. From there, descend the west basin: slabs first, then red scree and heather, then the boulder bottleneck, and finally the west rib and the dry creek bed, where deadfall slows everything. Expect devil's club near Hozomeen Creek before rejoining the Hozomeen Lake trail.
approach: From the Hozomeen Lake/Willow Lake trailhead at Hozomeen Campground (roughly 1,650-1,720 ft), a maintained trail runs 1.5 to several miles before climbers leave it near Hozomeen Lake's outlet, cross Hozomeen Creek, and push east through heavy deadfall and devil's club into the peak's west basin. This gains a rib/gully system leading to a high camp or bivy around 4,900-5,000 ft, and on to a saddle reported at roughly 6,800 ft below the final pitches.
overview: The first-ascent route on Hozomeen's South Peak, climbed by Fred Beckey's party in 1947; the South Peak is Washington's steepest summit by average angle, with a north face that is nearly vertical for 1,000 feet.
fa: Fred Beckey, Melvin Marcus, Jerry O'Neil, Ken Prestrud, Herb Staley, and Charles Welsh, May 30, 1947
